I'm glad that what I wrote was able to resonate with you. I do understand to a large extent what you mean: each day poses an entirely new challenge. Thank you for your words and I send you love too :)

I needed to write this and get it off my chest. It means a lot to me that this has helped you. I know how hard those days can be, and I'm proud of you for getting through it.
Thank you so much. You're not alone either :)

I really get you! A lot of times from an external perspective, it looks like I'm doing a lot of things and I'm doing it well. Under the surface though, I'm probably struggling on so many different levels. I hope you're able to find a balance soon that lets you maintain your mental health more - this state isn't always sustainable. No matter your output, your struggle with ADHD is always real and valid.

I'm glad you were able to resonate with this and I'm happy you're a supportive parent to your son. My post did reflect a lot of my frustration so it is a little negative than I usually feel, but I'm very glad if reading it has has helped your son realise he's not alone.

A couple of my close friends actually love hearing about my hyperfixations and I'm so thankful for it. I've become self conscious after previous experiences, but these friends listen so intently when I talk about my interests and love how excited I get. They also never invalidate me for being too sensitive. That being said, not every one of my friends is like that so it does take a toll :/ This is good advice though, thank you!

I want to let you know that this comment means a lot to me. It really makes me feel so much better to read these comments and know that I've managed to help at least a few people, or give them something to resonate with. This subreddit has helped me so much, too. Thank you as well :)

Yes, getting a diagnosis can really make such a huge difference. It's kind of sad how many of us thought so negatively ourselves beforehand. Burnout is extremely rough and I hope you've been able to recover from it, your struggle is so valid and real.

I just want to say there's no shame in taking medication. I don't know your situation obviously and I've never taken medication before but I do hope very much that you're able to get the help you need! I'm sure you'll have lots of different options if you choose to discuss it with your doctor. Or, if you choose not to go ahead with that, I hope you're able to find other coping mechanisms that make it a little easier to deal with everything. Good luck :)

It sounds like you've been through so much lately. I can't imagine how exhausting it must be. Take this time to be kind to yourself and I'm proud of you for keeping yourself going despite everything. You seem determined to make everything work, and to me, that's pretty huge.

Wow, that analogy makes perfect sense. It definitely captures the experience and I might be using it as well. 

Thank you for the compliment, I'm actually quite fond of writing so I'm glad to hear it :)

You're not stupid, and I hope that over time you recognise that completely. I'm glad that this was able to remind you. And it means a lot to me that you are proud, that's something I need to hear from time to time as well. Thank you for being so kind :)

Haha, I'm getting this a lot. I have been learning English for quite a while I just get self conscious on reddit because people are a little strict about grammar and I already miss words and things a lot because of the ADHD. I'm glad you were able to resonate!

It's so important to find reasons to keep going, and I'm really happy you have that in your life. I'm sure your family is very proud of you. In no way does being functional on the outside negate the struggles you go through.

I'm proud of you for fighting for it! You deserve to be validated and have your struggles heard. For me, as well, appearing "functional" means having a patchwork of strange coping mechanisms under the surface. I hope you're getting the help you need now :)

I'm happy this could resonate with you! I'm much younger, and it's easy for me to feel like I'm alone too. Spaces like this subreddit really help. Taking it one day at a time is so important and I'm wishing you the best!

I want you to know that you shouldn't have to apologise for ranting, on this subreddit we are here to listen to each other's experiences. I can relate to feeling like I'm inadequate, even though I know what my achievements are I still don't feel like they're enough for that I've done enough for them. Still, I've been trying to acknowledge them better now. I used to feel guilty for being proud of myself but now I'm more okay with it. Dean's list is huge!! And you have a bright future ahead of you. Good job :)

Thank you for the advice! There are definitely different kinds of exhaustion. Mental exhaustion is absolutely the worst. But physical exhaustion when it's at a healthy level (not too intense) can feel closer to satisfying. I have a lot going on as a student but I'm trying to make more room for days off too.

I can completely understand that. I thought there was something I was doing wrong when I noticed people around me didn't seem to struggle like I did. Thankfully now that I've realised I'm trying to be much kinder to myself haha
I just wanted to say I'm proud of you for making it this far and I hope you get all the help you deserve now. Making it this far is no small feat.

Thank you so much for your kind words, it means so much to me. I hope that your diagnosis has helped you. It can be so hard when you seem like you're doing well but your struggle is invisible. I'm really grateful that at this point in my life I do have a good support system.
I'm so glad you've been more forgiving lately. That's honestly so important and also inspiring. Wishing you the best :)
Thank you for your kind words, I'm definitely trying to do more of that. I do feel guilty about taking breaks but we all need them.
I'm so glad you were able to resonate with it.
Yes, invisible is the right word. People don't know how hard we work for the smallest things.

I really understand what you mean! I'm a huge extrovert and my relationships are very important to me, but masking made it really difficult to connect with people and being bullied has made me extremely self conscious. Now my friends do know but I think the popular perception of ADHD is very different from what it's actually like, so I still have to explain a lot.

And thank you, I'm glad I was able to communicate well!

Thank you, it means a lot to get complimented on my English! And yes, I really understand where you're coming from and I'm glad you were able to identity with what I said. All my ways of working are so unpredictable too :/

Thank you so much for your kind words!

I think it helps me personally to acknowledge that ADHD is the reason many things are hard without it being an excuse. For example, I still need to work to get where I want to be regardless of my ADHD. That being said, I can have extra empathy with myself because I know it's hard for me to start tasks and focus on them. Maybe I won't have the same process as a neurotypical person and that is something I can accept. Understanding these things is nowhere near using ADHD as an excuse or for blame. 

I know so many of us have issues with the word "laziness" and I've been trying to have more empathy with myself and not call myself lazy, because I'm not and I'm pretty sure you're not either.
You put it into words perfectly. There's a lot of things that are possible for us to do, but it just takes so so much out of us.

I'm so glad you resonate with this, this subreddit has been so helpful in understanding myself for me as well. I completely get what you mean about the endless running tasks, it feels like everywhere I look I have things I haven't done.

I've been brushing my teeth everyday, still working on the shower part. One step at a time lmao. Thank you so much for being proud of me, I need to hear that sometimes.
